title: Audit duplicate and absent keys
scenario: Esvani Inspection receives 32 invented sample records and a Limits table. A repeated product key in Limits is deliberately ambiguous; blank/unlisted keys are also present. Use a requirement only when exactly one matching specification row exists.

lesson.intro: A successful lookup is not evidence that a key is unique. Confirm cardinality first when duplicate specifications would make a decision ambiguous.

functions.name: XLOOKUP
functions.purpose: Find a key and return its corresponding value.
functions.arguments: Supply the key, aligned key and return ranges, optional missing label, match mode (0 exact, -1 next smaller, 1 next larger), and search direction (1 first, -1 last).
functions.mistake: Exact is the default. A first match does not aggregate duplicates. Binary search requires correctly sorted keys.

functions.name: INDEX
functions.purpose: Return the value at a row and column position.
functions.arguments: array contains values; row_num selects its row and optional column_num selects its column.
functions.useCase: Select an item in a specification matrix.
functions.mistake: Row positions are relative to the selected array, not worksheet row numbers.

functions.name: MATCH
functions.purpose: Find the relative position of a value.
functions.arguments: lookup_value is the key; lookup_array is one row or column; use match_type 0 for exact matching.
functions.useCase: Find a row or column position for INDEX.
functions.mistake: Omitting 0 requests approximate matching, which has ordering requirements.

lesson.combine: Reuse COUNTIFS and IF to require exactly one limit record. Then use XLOOKUP or INDEX/MATCH to retrieve it. IFERROR alone does not detect duplicates because a first-match lookup can succeed.

tasks.prompt: For the first six inspection rows, count matching Product_code entries in Limits, excluding its header.
Return the first unique product’s hardness limit using INDEX/MATCH.
For the first six rows, return the hardness limit only when exactly one Limits row matches; otherwise return Review key.
For the first six rows, return Pass for hardness at most a unique limit, Hold above it, or Review key for any ambiguous/absent key.

bonus.prompt: Count Limits rows with product EX-2.
